entries.he: מִי שֶׁנִּפְתָּה לִבּוֹ לִגְזֹל וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהִתִּיר לְעַצְמוֹ גְּזֵלַת חֲבֵרוֹ, הֲרֵי הוּא מוּכָן לְכָל חֵטְא וְעָוֹן, וְאֵין תַּקָּנָה לַהֲסִירוֹ מִדַּרְכּוֹ הָרָעָה.
entries.en: 1. One whose heart is tempted to steal (openly), since he has permitted himself to steal from his fellow, he is poised to commit any sin, and there is no remedy to turn him away from his evil way.

entries.he: בַּעֲווֹן הַגֶּזֶל הַגּוּבַאי עוֹלֶה וְרָעָב הֲוָה וּבְנֵי־אָדָם אוֹכְלִין בְּשַׂר־בְּנֵיהֶם.
entries.en: 2. Through the sin of stealing, the locusts arise, and there is famine, and people eat the flesh of their children.

entries.en: 3. Someone who does not benefit others with his money, through this robbers come upon him.

entries.he: הַגּוֹזֵל אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ שְׁוֵה פְּרוּטָה, כְּאִלּוּ נוֹטֵל נִשְׁמָתוֹ וְנִשְׁמַת בָּנָיו וּבְנוֹתָיו, וַאֲפִלּוּ גְּרָמָא.
entries.en: 4. One who steals the worth of a penny from his fellow, it is as if he takes away his soul, and the soul of his sons and daughters, and even (if he stole) indirectly.

entries.en: 5. Someone who does not have regard for his friend's money, it is certain that he is a thief.
